title: Furthest Building You Can Reach
summary: Given an array of building heights, a number of bricks, and ladders, determine the furthest building index you can reach by optimally using the bricks and ladders.
statement: Given an array of building heights, a number of bricks, and ladders, determine the furthest building index you can reach by optimally using the bricks and ladders. If the next building is taller, you can either use one ladder or the difference in height in bricks. If the current building is taller or equal, no additional items are needed.
constraints: 1–100,000 buildings; bricks and ladders are nonnegative.
Descending moves are free. Spend ladders on the largest positive climbs encountered and bricks on the others.
hints: Among climbs seen so far, ladders should cover the largest ones.
Put every positive climb in a min-heap; when there are too many for the ladders, pay bricks for the smallest.
Process edges in order and stop before the first payment that makes bricks negative.
Exchanging a ladder from a smaller climb to a larger one never uses more bricks, proving the heap allocation is optimal.
editorial: Exchanging a ladder from a smaller climb to a larger one never uses more bricks, proving the heap allocation is optimal.

tests.explanation: Using bricks for climbs five and three leaves no resources for the next climb five, so index four is furthest.
Optimal resource assignment reaches index seven.
